items.t: Enbridge stock: Scotiabank cuts EPS forecast as bond deal advances
sum: Enbridge faced a lower earnings forecast from Scotiabank during the week of November 9-13, while a separate report outlined a USD3.2 billion bond financing scheduled for delivery on Friday, November 13. The developments add analyst caution and financing activity to the Canadian energy infrastructure group's recent quarterly update.

MarketBeat reported on Friday, November 13, that Scotiabank had lowered its Enbridge earnings estimate in a report released on Wednesday, November 11. The bank reduced its forecast from 2.08 to 2.04 US dollars per share and kept a Strong Buy rating.

The revised forecast was below the consensus estimate cited by MarketBeat. The change followed Enbridge's third-quarter results on November 6, which the report said had exceeded the consensus quarterly earnings estimate.

Krugman Insights reported on Friday, November 13, that Enbridge had set delivery for a USD3.2 billion transaction spanning five senior and fixed-reset subordinated bond tranches. The report described the financing as in progress, so the scheduled delivery should not be confused with a completed transaction.

For investors, the combination of a reduced external earnings forecast and new financing activity keeps attention on Enbridge's earnings trajectory, capital needs and balance-sheet management. The two developments address different parts of the investment case: one changes an analyst expectation, while the other concerns funding for the company's operations and projects.

The latest developments come after Enbridge reaffirmed its full-year outlook with its third-quarter results. The analyst revision does not itself establish a change in company guidance, while the bond report describes financing terms and timing rather than a change to operating targets.

Market participants will next focus on the company's execution against its outlook, project spending and financing costs. The Canadian energy infrastructure sector remains relevant for broader current market reports.

items.t: Enbridge stock posts stronger Q3 as 2026 guidance stays intact
sum: Enbridge reported stronger third-quarter results on November 6, 2026, and reaffirmed its full-year outlook. In its earnings release, the Canadian energy infrastructure group said adjusted EBITDA reached CAD 4.434 billion for the three months ended September 30, compared with CAD 4.267 billion a year earlier. Distributable cash flow increased to CAD 2.689 billion from CAD 2.566 billion.

Adjusted earnings rose to CAD 1.074 billion, or CAD 0.49 per common share, from CAD 997 million, or CAD 0.46 per share. GAAP earnings attributable to common shareholders were CAD 1.288 billion, or CAD 0.59 per share, versus CAD 682 million, or CAD 0.30 per share in the prior-year quarter.

Enbridge said the increase in GAAP earnings was driven partly by non-cash, unrealized changes in derivative values used for foreign-exchange, interest-rate and commodity-price risk management. The company also noted that adjusted EBITDA benefited from higher revenues following rate settlements and rate increases in gas transmission and gas distribution. Those gains more than offset lower market-access volumes in Liquids Pipelines and lower tolls on Line 9 deliveries.

Management kept its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance at CAD 20.2 billion to CAD 20.8 billion and its distributable cash flow guidance at CAD 5.70 to CAD 6.10 per share. Enbridge also maintained a medium-term outlook for average annual growth of approximately 5 percent in adjusted EBITDA, distributable cash flow per share and earnings per share.

The company said its secured growth backlog stood at approximately CAD 38 billion after more than CAD 3 billion of gas transmission projects entered service during the quarter. Enbridge is targeting CAD 10 billion to CAD 20 billion of new project announcements through 2027 and expects annual growth investment capacity of CAD 10 billion to CAD 11 billion.

Enbridge announced the acquisition of Tallgrass Energy's crude oil business for USD 2.55 billion. The assets include interests in the Pony Express Pipeline and Powder River Gateway system, storage capacity and the Stanchion crude marketing business. The associated Pony Express 2 project would expand capacity and is expected to enter service in late 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions.

sum: Enbridge reported stronger third-quarter results on November 6, 2026, and reaffirmed its full-year financial guidance. The Enbridge news release said adjusted earnings increased to 1.1 billion Canadian dollars from 1.0 billion Canadian dollars a year earlier, while adjusted earnings per share rose to 0.49 Canadian dollars from 0.46 Canadian dollars.

Adjusted EBITDA reached 4.434 billion Canadian dollars, up from 4.267 billion Canadian dollars in the third quarter of 2025. Distributable cash flow rose to 2.689 billion Canadian dollars from 2.566 billion Canadian dollars, although cash from operating activities declined to 2.703 billion Canadian dollars from 2.868 billion Canadian dollars.

Gas Transmission was the strongest contributor to the operating improvement. Its adjusted EBITDA increased to 1.427 billion Canadian dollars from 1.262 billion Canadian dollars, supported by rate settlements, a previously approved rate increase at Texas Eastern and higher allowance for equity funds used during construction.

Gas Distribution and Storage also advanced, with adjusted EBITDA rising to 665 million Canadian dollars from 560 million Canadian dollars. Enbridge attributed the gain mainly to higher base rates at Enbridge Gas Utah and Enbridge Gas North Carolina, as well as higher distribution margins and customer growth at Enbridge Gas Ontario.

Liquids Pipelines remained a drag on the quarterly mix. Adjusted EBITDA fell to 2.206 billion Canadian dollars from 2.307 billion Canadian dollars because of lower Mainline volumes, lower Line 9 tolls and weaker Market Access contributions. The company also said higher interest expense and depreciation from newly completed assets partly offset the improvement in adjusted earnings.

Enbridge reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of 20.2 billion to 20.8 billion Canadian dollars and distributable cash flow per share guidance of 5.70 to 6.10 Canadian dollars. Management also maintained its medium-term target for average annual growth of about 5% in adjusted EBITDA, distributable cash flow per share and earnings per share.
The company placed the Aspen Point expansion of the British Columbia Pipeline and the Tennessee Ridgeline project into service during the quarter.

This is the Stock I’m Retiring On: It’s Already Up 17.67% Since 2021
sum: We just published our list of the 10 Stocks I Am Retiring On, and Enbridge Inc. (NYSE:ENB) ranked 10th on the list.

A retirement portfolio needs businesses that can keep rewarding shareholders long after the current market narrative fades. Dividends show how important those quieter sources of return can be: according to S&P Dow Jones Indices research cited in our coverage of Dividend Aristocrat stocks, dividends have accounted for roughly 31% of the S&P 500's total return since 1926, with capital appreciation accounting for the remaining 69%. In the 1940s and 1970s, dividend income accounted for more than half of total returns. The lesson is not that every retirement investment must pay dividends, but rather that long-term shareholder gains can come from sources other than rising share prices.

Warren Buffett offers a useful test for that level of dedication. He has advised investors to buy only what they would "perfectly happy to hold if the market shut down for 10 years." Rather than relying on the potential to sell tomorrow, investors should consider how much the underlying business may make over a decade. That business-owner perspective is the common thread running through Insider Monkey's discussion of Warren Buffett's best long-term stocks to buy.

For retirement investors, the distinction between a high starting dividend and an increasing dividend is crucial. The S&P 500 Dividend Aristocrats index requires components to have increased dividends for at least 25 years in a row. This is a record that spans numerous economic cycles, though it doesn't guarantee future growth. Insider Monkey's analysis of dividend growth stocks to buy and hold in 2026 looked at 68 such companies and evaluated their five-year average dividend growth rates.

Of course, financial strength is just as important as payout record. A dividend competes with debt repayments, capital spending, and other financial requirements. Liabilities are broader than debt, but the comparison shows the type of liquidity cushion worth considering alongside dividend yield.

Enbridge earned its place on the list after The Motley Fool's Matt DiLallo named it a stock he planned to buy in his retirement account, while Seeking Alpha's Leo Nelissen included it in his 20-stock model retirement portfolio.

How Much Would You Need to Invest in Enbridge to Average $200 a Month?
sum: A company helping deliver energy to your home can also help pay the bills. The appealing part is getting cash without selling shares every month. The less attractive part is building the holding first. At the current payment and recent closing price, roughly $42,600 in one pipeline stock could produce a $200 monthly average, with the cash arriving quarterly.

A $200 monthly average means $2,400 a year. For a stock paying every three months, the practical target is about $600 each quarter. I’d collect the dividends in cash and make monthly transfers from that balance, giving my spending a smoother schedule than the company’s payment calendar.

Enbridge (TSX: ENB) makes that calculation possible with a quarterly dividend of $0.97 per share. Its annualized $3.88 payment yields about 5.6% at the recent closing price of $68.82. That’s substantial starting income, so the next step is making sure the business has room to pay it.

Enbridge operates oil and natural gas pipelines, gas utilities, and other energy infrastructure. Much of its earnings relies on regulated returns or contracted service, giving it a different relationship with oil prices from a producer selling the commodity. Customers pay for access to infrastructure they need to move and use energy.

Utilities and export facilities needing more gas capacity offer growth opportunities. Enbridge’s second-quarter update described new pipeline connections and expansions supported by customer demand. New assets can add earnings once operating, although construction spending comes before those earnings arrive.

For the dividend, management reaffirmed 2026 distributable cash flow of $5.70 to $6.10 per share. This is the company’s cash-flow measure after adjustments including maintenance spending and financing costs. The $3.88 annual dividend uses roughly 64% to 68% of that range, leaving some cash beyond the payment.
Reaching at least $2,400 annually requires 619 whole shares at the current payment. Using the recent close, and excluding trading fees, here’s the investment required.

items.t: Inflation Is Heading to 3.5%: Yet These 2 Canadian Stocks Can Raise Prices and Keep Their Customers
sum: Canadians do not need a spreadsheet to know that prices are on the rise. They notice these trends at the pump and the grocery checkout.

Statistics Canada reported that consumer prices rose 3.1% year over year in September, up from 3.0% in August. On October 28, the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate by a quarter point to 2.50%, its first hike since July 2023.
The central bank also expects inflation to reach about 3.5% by the end of 2026. Moreover, the regulator does not see a return to its 2% target until mid-2028.
Given this macro backdrop, let’s see which companies are well positioned to pass higher costs to customers.
The Bank of Canada says inflation excluding gasoline was 2.2% in September, and the core measure remains close to 2%.
However, the central bank says high fuel prices are lifting production and transportation costs, which have been primarily absorbed by businesses.
Notably, companies that do not enjoy pricing power have seen profit margins shrink over the last six months.

Enbridge Announces CDN$2.6 Billion Bought-Deal Offering of Common Shares
sum: The Canadian base shelf prospectus is accessible, and the Canadian prospectus supplement or any amendment will be accessible, within two business days through SEDAR+.

CALGARY, AB, Sept. 9, 2026 /CNW/ -- Enbridge Inc. (TSX: ENB) (NYSE: ENB) ("Enbridge" or the "Company") today announced that it has entered into an agreement with a syndicate of underwriters (the "Underwriters") led by RBC Capital Markets and CIBC Capital Markets, and including Scotiabank, BMO Capital Markets, TD Securities Inc., and National Bank of Canada Capital Markets as joint bookrunners, under which the Underwriters have agreed to purchase, on a bought deal basis, 38,900,000 common shares of the Company ("Common Shares") for aggregate gross proceeds of CDN$2.6 billion at an offering price of CDN$66.85 per Common Share (the "Offering").

Enbridge intends to use the net proceeds from the Offering to partially fund announced acquisitions and to create financial flexibility to fund potential future growth opportunities. A portion of the net proceeds of the Offering may be temporarily used to reduce indebtedness or invested in short-term liquid investments.

The Common Shares will be offered to the public in all of the provinces of Canada through the Underwriters and their affiliates by way of a Canadian prospectus supplement (the "Canadian Prospectus Supplement") to Enbridge's short form base shelf prospectus dated September 9, 2026 (the "Canadian Prospectus"). The Common Shares will be offered to the public in the United States pursuant to Enbridge's registration statement, including a prospectus (the "U.S. Prospectus"), filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"), and a prospectus supplement (the "U.S. Prospectus Supplement") to the U.S. Prospectus. Before investing, prospective purchasers in Canada should read the Canadian Prospectus Supplement, the Canadian Prospectus and the documents incorporated by reference therein, and prospective purchasers in the United States should read the U.S. Prospectus, the U.S. Prospectus Supplement and the documents incorporated by reference therein for more complete information about Enbridge and the Offering in Canada and the United States, respectively.

Here’s Where Enbridge Stock Could Be Headed in the Next 3 Years
sum: Enbridge (TSX: ENB) has been on a roll for the past 30 months. Investors who missed the rebound are wondering if ENB stock is still undervalued and good to buy for a self-directed Tax-Free Savings Account (TFSA) or Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) portfolio focused on dividends and total returns.
Enbridge trades near $72.50 per share at the time of writing. The stock was as low as $43 in late 2023 and isn’t far off the recent record high above $77.

In order to get a sense of where the stock might be headed in the next few years, it is important to look at the reason the stock pulled back through the second half of 2022 and most of 2023 before reversing course.

Investors will recall that the Bank of Canada and the U.S. Federal Reserve started to raise interest rates in 2022 and continued the rate increases through 2023 in an effort to get inflation under control. Enbridge and its energy infrastructure peers use debt to fund growth investments, including acquisitions and capital projects. The steep rise in borrowing costs that occurred over such a short period of time caused concern among investors who worried that a spike in debt expenses would hurt profits and cut into cash flow that could be used to reduce debt and pay dividends. Some pundits even speculated that Enbridge’s generous dividend would be at risk of being cut to preserve cash.

The recovery in the share price began around the time the central banks indicated they were done raising interest rates. Bargain hunters moved into the stock, anticipating rate cuts in 2024 and 2025. These reductions materialized, helping push ENB even higher.

Earlier this year, the market broadly expected additional rate cuts for 2026. That might not happen as soaring oil prices are putting upward pressure on inflation. Analysts are now starting to warn that rate increases might be needed in Canada and the United States if inflation jumps in the coming months. In that scenario, Enbridge’s stock price would face new headwinds.
Enbridge is offsetting the impact of higher interest rates by growing revenue and earnings. The company spent US$14 billion in 2024 to buy three American natural gas utilities.

Suncor, Enbridge, or Canadian Natural — Which Oil Stock Fits Your Portfolio Best?
sum: Canadian oil stocks used to be a filthy asset class. However, since 2020, these stocks have steadily been gaining popularity with both retail and institutional investors.

In the past five years, the sector has significantly consolidated and outperformed. The best producers drastically reduced debt and cleaned up their balance sheets. Likewise, they focused on the most economic assets and drilling opportunities.

As result, Canadian oil stocks are lean, cash flow machines. Since the Iran war pushed oil prices skyward, Canadian oil stocks are set to enjoy a major windfall. Suncor Enbridge (TSX: SU), Enbridge (TSX: ENB), and Canadian Natural Resources (TSX: CNQ) are some of Canada’s best known energy stocks. Here’s why each has its investment merits and why you might want to prefer one over the other.

With a market cap of $104 billion, Suncor Energy is Canada’s top integrated oil stock. It produces 855,000 barrels of oil per day and refines 466,000 barrels of oil per day. It also has a large retail distribution network through 1,640 Petro-Canada retail locations and 320 commercial Cardlock locations.
Suncor’s stock lagged for several years due to underperforming operations and safety issues. However, its new management has largely cleaned up the business.

With a strong balance sheet today and a mix of long-life assets (25 years of reserves), Suncor has committed to returning 100% of its excess cash flows to shareholders. It has also committed to growing its dividend by 3-5% per year. It yields 2.73% today.
This is a good stock if you want a diversified mix of assets that generate strong cash flows. While this oil stock has a lower yield, capital returns will come as it steadily retires its share count.

This Energy Stock Pays a 5.8% Dividend (And It's Safe)
sum: - The pipeline and utility company has very conservative financial metrics.
- It has plenty of fuel to invest in growing its operations while continuing to increase its high-yielding dividend.
Enbridge (NYSE: ENB) entered 2026 with a 5.8% dividend yield. That's several times higher than the S&P 500's yield, which is near a record low at around 1.1%.
While higher-yielding dividend stocks can have a higher risk profile, that's not the case with Enbridge. Its high-yielding dividend is very safe.
Enbridge has paid dividends for more than 70 years. The company recently announced plans to increase its payment by 3% for 2026, marking its 31st consecutive year of dividend raises.

The Canadian pipeline and utility company generates very stable and predictable cash flow. Roughly 98% of its cash flows come from cost-of-service agreements or long-term, fixed-fee contracts. Enbridge's earnings are so predictable that it has achieved its annual financial guidance for 19 years in a row.

Enbridge pays out 60%-70% of its stable cash flow in dividends, enabling it to retain billions of dollars annually. The company also has a strong investment-grade balance sheet, backed by a leverage ratio within its target range of 4.5-5.0 times. As a result, Enbridge has ample financial flexibility to fund organic expansion projects and make bolt-on acquisitions.
